messages.content: You are one member of a parallel architecture inquiry. Return only the contracted JSON. Produce executable mechanisms, APIs, state transitions, and verification rules; do not propose organizational process or prose-only governance.

Evidence: 84 Claude sessions in five days manually performed environment diagnosis, repository archaeology, architecture reconstruction, research synthesis, Lean proof work, refactors, tests, memory/skill creation, and repeated failure analysis. A transcript audit counted 2,067 direct mutations versus 190 subagent dispatches and about 30% human corrections. Prior harness research specifies carrier adapters with zero substrate intelligence, append-only prompt/tool/result capture, projected memory/context, deterministic tools, governed consolidation only after results, session heartbeats, work claim/settle, and context-compaction continuity. The existing free-compute-dev seed has deterministic resolver -> context -> model edit -> apply -> test -> feedback rounds -> expensive escalation, but only one task and no autonomous intake/decomposition/fanout/tool navigation/isolation/integration/memory. The existing LISS cheapest-sufficient fabric just demonstrated 24/24 schema-verified jobs at 24.45 useful jobs/min across Gemini and GitHub Models, with OpenRouter fallback and Claude available. Future volunteer CPU/GPU endpoints can join over Tailscale. The target is a Union-owned software-production fabric that receives territories/problems and keeps observing, decomposing, executing, verifying, integrating, and learning without a Codex or Claude conversation carrying the work.

Your bounded question: Design the cheapest-provider tool-using coding worker protocol: bounded read/search/edit/test actions over an isolated workspace, with no provider-native tools required.

State what is absent from the current seed, give a concrete design, and name a smallest real vertical slice.

completion.text: {"component":"CheapProviderToolWorker","absentMechanism":"The current seed executes one model→edit→apply→test round with no multi-turn tool loop. Missing: (1) a text-protocol tool parser so any completion endpoint works without provider function-calling APIs; (2) workspace isolation — per-task tmpdir copy so failed attempts don't corrupt the repo; (3) tool result injection — appending structured results back into the prompt sequence; (4) a budget governor counting steps against a max_steps cap; (5) any ability for the model to read or search the repo before committing an edit. The model currently edits blind.","design":["System prompt encodes all tools as plain-text schema with call/result examples — no API function schema, so any completion endpoint works: Gemini free, GitHub Models, OpenRouter cheapest tier, or Claude.","Tool call format uses minimal XML tags the harness parses with a single regex: <tool>name</tool><arg1>val</arg1>... One tool call per model turn; harness rejects and re-prompts if multiple are emitted.","Six deterministic tools: read_file(path, start_line?, end_line?) → text; list_dir(path) → names; search(pattern, path) → grep -n output; edit_file(path, old_exact, new_exact) → ok | no_match; write_file(path, content) → ok; run_test(cmd) → {exit_code, stdout, stderr} all truncated to 2 KB.","Workspace: on task claim, copy declared file set into an isolated tmpdir. All tool paths are validated against tmpdir prefix — path traversal returns path_violation, never executes.","Harness loop: call model → scan output for tool tags → dispatch → append <tool_result> block to context → repeat until (a) model emits no tool tag (final answer), (b) run_test exit_code==0, or (c) steps_used == max_steps.","Budget governor: max_steps is a job-level config (default 20). On exhaustion the harness emits a partial result record with escalate:true and last workspace diff, consumable by the LISS escalation path.","Duplicate-call detector: if (tool, canonical_args) repeats twice, harness injects 'already returned this result' without re-executing, decrement budget by 1 to break loops.","Result record schema: {job_id, steps_used, exit_code, diff_patch, cost_tokens, escalate, error?} — typed and schema-verified the same way LISS currently verifies its 24/24 jobs."],"firstVerticalSlice":["Write the six tool dispatcher functions (pure Python, no subprocess except run_test) with tmpdir-prefix enforcement as the only security boundary.","Write the regex tool-call parser: extract tool name and all sibling arg tags from a completion string; return ParseError if malformed.","Write the system prompt template: header, tool catalog with one call+result example each, task slot, and explicit instruction to emit exactly one tool call or a final ANSWER: block.","Wire into one LISS job type 'tool_worker_task': claim job → copy file_set to tmpdir → run harness loop → emit result record → settle job.","Smoke test: job payload = {task: 'add a return-type annotation to function parse_entry in parser.py', file_set: ['parser.py', 'test_parser.py'], test_cmd: 'pytest test_parser.py -q'}. Assert: worker reads parser.py, edits it, runs pytest, result record has exit_code=0, diff_patch non-empty, steps_used ≤ 20."],"failureModes":["Malformed tool syntax: parser returns ParseError; harness injects error as tool_result and continues loop — model self-corrects on next turn without burning a subprocess call.","run_test hangs: subprocess runs under a timeout (default 30 s); on expiry returns {exit_code: -1, stderr: 'timeout_exceeded'} and counts as one step.","edit_file no_match: model used wrong exact string; harness returns no_match, model must re-read then retry — duplicate-call detector prevents infinite read loops.","Context window saturation before budget exhausted: harness tracks estimated token count; at 80% of provider limit it stops the loop, sets escalate:true, and emits partial result.","Path traversal attempt: any resolved path outside tmpdir returns path_violation immediately; logged to result record for audit; loop continues."],"successMetric":"One worker, given a task and file set, completes read→edit→test in ≤20 text-protocol tool steps with no provider function-calling API, emits a schema-valid result record (diff_patch, exit_code, steps_used, cost_tokens), and passes the repo's own test suite on Gemini free tier and GitHub Models free tier."}

structured_output.absentMechanism: The current seed executes one model→edit→apply→test round with no multi-turn tool loop. Missing: (1) a text-protocol tool parser so any completion endpoint works without provider function-calling APIs; (2) workspace isolation — per-task tmpdir copy so failed attempts don't corrupt the repo; (3) tool result injection — appending structured results back into the prompt sequence; (4) a budget governor counting steps against a max_steps cap; (5) any ability for the model to read or search the repo before committing an edit. The model currently edits blind.
design: System prompt encodes all tools as plain-text schema with call/result examples — no API function schema, so any completion endpoint works: Gemini free, GitHub Models, OpenRouter cheapest tier, or Claude.

Tool call format uses minimal XML tags the harness parses with a single regex: <tool>name</tool><arg1>val</arg1>... One tool call per model turn; harness rejects and re-prompts if multiple are emitted.

Six deterministic tools: read_file(path, start_line?, end_line?) → text; list_dir(path) → names; search(pattern, path) → grep -n output; edit_file(path, old_exact, new_exact) → ok | no_match; write_file(path, content) → ok; run_test(cmd) → {exit_code, stdout, stderr} all truncated to 2 KB.
Workspace: on task claim, copy declared file set into an isolated tmpdir. All tool paths are validated against tmpdir prefix — path traversal returns path_violation, never executes.

Harness loop: call model → scan output for tool tags → dispatch → append <tool_result> block to context → repeat until (a) model emits no tool tag (final answer), (b) run_test exit_code==0, or (c) steps_used == max_steps.

Budget governor: max_steps is a job-level config (default 20). On exhaustion the harness emits a partial result record with escalate:true and last workspace diff, consumable by the LISS escalation path.
Duplicate-call detector: if (tool, canonical_args) repeats twice, harness injects 'already returned this result' without re-executing, decrement budget by 1 to break loops.
Result record schema: {job_id, steps_used, exit_code, diff_patch, cost_tokens, escalate, error?} — typed and schema-verified the same way LISS currently verifies its 24/24 jobs.
firstVerticalSlice: Write the six tool dispatcher functions (pure Python, no subprocess except run_test) with tmpdir-prefix enforcement as the only security boundary.
Write the regex tool-call parser: extract tool name and all sibling arg tags from a completion string; return ParseError if malformed.
Write the system prompt template: header, tool catalog with one call+result example each, task slot, and explicit instruction to emit exactly one tool call or a final ANSWER: block.
Wire into one LISS job type 'tool_worker_task': claim job → copy file_set to tmpdir → run harness loop → emit result record → settle job.

Smoke test: job payload = {task: 'add a return-type annotation to function parse_entry in parser.py', file_set: ['parser.py', 'test_parser.py'], test_cmd: 'pytest test_parser.py -q'}. Assert: worker reads parser.py, edits it, runs pytest, result record has exit_code=0, diff_patch non-empty, steps_used ≤ 20.
failureModes: Malformed tool syntax: parser returns ParseError; harness injects error as tool_result and continues loop — model self-corrects on next turn without burning a subprocess call.
run_test hangs: subprocess runs under a timeout (default 30 s); on expiry returns {exit_code: -1, stderr: 'timeout_exceeded'} and counts as one step.
edit_file no_match: model used wrong exact string; harness returns no_match, model must re-read then retry — duplicate-call detector prevents infinite read loops.
Context window saturation before budget exhausted: harness tracks estimated token count; at 80% of provider limit it stops the loop, sets escalate:true, and emits partial result.
Path traversal attempt: any resolved path outside tmpdir returns path_violation immediately; logged to result record for audit; loop continues.
structured_output.successMetric: One worker, given a task and file set, completes read→edit→test in ≤20 text-protocol tool steps with no provider function-calling API, emits a schema-valid result record (diff_patch, exit_code, steps_used, cost_tokens), and passes the repo's own test suite on Gemini free tier and GitHub Models free tier.
